rows.citation: Luu QH, Liu H, Chen TY, et al. (2022). Testing ocean software with metamorphic testing. Proceedings of the 7th International Workshop on Metamorphic Testing (MET '22), ACM, pp. 23-30.
rows.model_type: tidal analysis and prediction scientific software (UTide, Python); geophysical time-series harmonic fitting, non-neuronal
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - 38 non-equivalent mutants from five operator sets seeded into UTide's solver; equivalents filtered by random tests plus manual inspection.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - seven metamorphic relations applied over 100 randomly generated synthetic tide time series.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - compares fitted tidal amplitudes and phases within a fixed 0.01 round-off, not neuronal features.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - compares per-relation mutation scores and says choosing the most effective relations matters, but performs no selection or minimisation.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - one subject program; relations and mutants evaluated together, no held-out programs or mutation families.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-assisted edits or transformations studied.
rows.software: none released identified; subject program UTide https://github.com/wesleybowman/UTide (URL as printed in the paper)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Methodologically the closest in this batch: seeded mutants plus several relations on scientific software, with relation effectiveness compared. NeuroSem would add neuron models, refinement-calibrated eFEL feature tolerances instead of a fixed round-off, greedy battery selection against cost-matched random sets, and held-out models and a held-out mutation family.
rows.verification_method: Crossref https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1145/3524846.3527341 (title, 4 authors, MET proceedings, pp. 23-30, issued 2022-05-09); OpenAlex https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.1145/3524846.3527341 (abstract); Semantic Scholar graph API batch (arXiv 2206.05457, DBLP conf/icse-met/LuuLCV22); full text read from https://arxiv.org/pdf/2206.05457 (v1).

rows.citation: Chen TY, Feng J, Tse TH (2002). Metamorphic testing of programs on partial differential equations: a case study. Proceedings 26th Annual International Computer Software and Applications (CMPSAC-02, Oxford, UK), IEEE Computer Society, pp. 327-333.
rows.model_type: numerical PDE solver program (elliptic PDE with Dirichlet boundary conditions, iterative finite-difference scheme); general scientific software
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - one hand-injected fault (a swapped variable in the convergence check) used for illustration; no systematic mutant generation.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - same problem solved on successively refined mesh grids and checked at several grid points; not distinct stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - checks computed temperatures at grid points, not neuronal or electrophysiological features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - a single metamorphic relation; no test selection or optimisation.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - single program and single seeded fault case study.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Early precedent for using behaviour under grid or step-size refinement as an oracle for numerical programs. NeuroSem would use refinement for a different job, calibrating feature tolerances, and would add neuron-specific stimulation protocols, systematic single-fault mutants, battery selection and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1109/cmpsac.2002.1045022 (title, authors, pp. 327-333, event CMPSAC-02 Oxford UK; no issued date); Semantic Scholar graph API batch (publicationDate 2002-08-26, DBLP conf/compsac/ChenFT02); figshare API https://api.figshare.com/v2/articles/26285137 (repository citation year 2002). OpenAlex https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.1109/cmpsac.2002.1045022 gives 2003, likely an indexing date; year 2002 adopted from the event and two concordant sources. Full text read from https://ndownloader.figshare.com/files/47650609.

rows.citation: Ahlgren J, Berezin M, Bojarczuk K, et al. (2021). Testing Web Enabled Simulation at Scale Using Metamorphic Testing. 2021 IEEE/ACM 43rd International Conference on Software Engineering: Software Engineering in Practice (ICSE-SEIP), IEEE, pp. 140-149.
rows.model_type: industrial multi-agent web-enabled simulation (Facebook WW with ML-trained bots); general software, non-biological
rows.controlled_mutations: no - no mutation analysis or fault seeding reported; evidence is deployment experience, flakiness measurements and bugs found.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - over 40 metamorphic tests across bot personas and mechanisms; regression framed as a relation between previous and latest versions.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - compares bot trajectories and platform behaviour, not neuronal features.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - a time-bounded test subset runs in CI and order-dependent tests are scheduled, but no fault-detection-driven selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - industrial experience report; no held-out systems or fault families.
rows.ai_transformations: no - simulated bots are ML-trained, but code changes under test are human-submitted diffs; AI-generated edits not studied.
rows.software: MIA (internal Facebook system; no public release identified)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shares version-to-version behavioural regression on a simulation, with repeated runs to judge flakiness. NeuroSem targets deterministic neuron models and would add seeded single-fault mutants, refinement-calibrated feature tolerances, an optimised stimulation battery compared with canonical and random baselines, and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1109/icse-seip52600.2021.00023 (title, 12 authors, pp. 140-149, issued 2021-05); OpenAlex https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.1109/icse-seip52600.2021.00023 (abstract); Semantic Scholar graph API batch (DBLP conf/icse/AhlgrenBBDDGGHL21); full text read from https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/10139790/1/SEIP21.pdf.
rows.found_via: WebSearch site:ieeexplore.ieee.org increasing validity of simulation models through metamorphic testing; verified via Crossref

rows.citation: Segura S, Fraser G, Sanchez AB, et al. (2016). A Survey on Metamorphic Testing. IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering 42(9):805-824.
rows.model_type: general software-testing survey (domains include simulation, bioinformatics, epidemiological models, machine learning)
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - surveys studies that evaluate metamorphic relations with seeded faults and mutants; the survey runs no mutation experiment itself.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - covers sets of metamorphic relations and source/follow-up test cases; no neuronal stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - no neuronal or electrophysiological feature extraction discussed; no neuroscience terms found in full text.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - names prioritisation and minimisation of metamorphic relations an open challenge, citing coverage- and similarity-based approaches.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - literature survey; analyses empirical practice but performs no held-out evaluation.
rows.ai_transformations: no - machine-learning programs appear only as test subjects; no AI-generated code transformations.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Canonical background showing that metamorphic testing, mutant-based evaluation of relations and relation prioritisation are established and cannot be claimed by NeuroSem. NeuroSem's candidate contribution would be the neuron-model-specific integration with calibrated feature tolerances, protocol-battery selection and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1109/tse.2016.2532875 (title, 4 authors, vol 42 issue 9 pp. 805-824, issued 2016-09-01); OpenAlex https://api.openalex.org/works/doi:10.1109/tse.2016.2532875 (abstract); Semantic Scholar graph API batch (DBLP journals/tse/SeguraFSC16; dblp.org itself returned an Anubis bot check); full text read from idUS repository https://idus.us.es/bitstreams/d8fffc33-4eb5-4bb4-a3d6-c4ddab3f7cb6/download (handle https://idus.us.es/handle/11441/38271).

rows.citation: Stacy B, Hauzel J, Lindvall M, et al. (2022). Metamorphic testing in bioinformatics software: a case study on metagenomic assembly. Proceedings of the 7th International Workshop on Metamorphic Testing (MET '22), ACM, pp. 31-33.
rows.model_type: general bioinformatics software (metagenomic assembly tools MEGAHIT and Pilon used by MetaCompass); not a mechanistic simulation model
rows.controlled_mutations: no - abstract reports a metamorphic test exposing real inconsistencies; no fault seeding mentioned (full text inaccessible, HTTP 403).
rows.multiple_stimuli: unclear - abstract describes one simple metamorphic test; variety of input transformations not stated.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - outputs are genome assemblies, not voltage traces or electrophysiological features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no test selection or optimisation described in abstract.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - short case study; no held-out subjects or fault families reported in abstract.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-assisted edits or transformations mentioned.
rows.software: none (tests MEGAHIT and Pilon; no testing-tool release identified)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shows metamorphic testing can find subtle defects in bioinformatics code that standard testing missed, which supports NeuroSem's motivation. NeuroSem would instead target neuron models, with seeded single-fault mutants, calibrated electrophysiology-feature tolerances and optimised multi-protocol batteries evaluated on held-out models.

rows.citation: Gürcan Ö, Dikenelli O, Bernon C (2014). A generic testing framework for agent-based simulation models. In: Agent-Based Modeling and Simulation, Palgrave Macmillan UK, pp. 231-270.
rows.model_type: agent-based simulation models (generic ABMS verification and validation); non-neuronal
rows.controlled_mutations: unclear - abstract describes a V&V testing framework and case study; no fault seeding mentioned; full text inaccessible.
rows.multiple_stimuli: unclear - abstract does not say whether multiple scenarios or input conditions are systematically run.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - agent-based simulation outputs, not electrophysiology.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no test selection or optimisation mentioned in abstract.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - abstract reports applicability on a single realistic case study.
rows.software: unverified (framework name and repository not retrieved)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Offers a general framework for testing and validating agent-based models. NeuroSem is narrower and more quantitative: neuron models, electrophysiology features, seeded single-fault mutants, calibrated tolerances, protocol-battery selection and held-out evaluation. This chapter appears to be the Journal of Simulation 2013 article (doi 10.1057/jos.2012.26) republished with the same title, authors and abstract.
